title: Prefill heartbeat and lazy-decode grafting to reduce prefill-decode stalls
author: Sofia Rivera
release_notes: Introduces prefill heartbeat and lazy-decode grafting to reduce tail latency by improving stage handover and KV priming; no user-facing API changes; recommended rollout on Dedicated first.
description: Motivation: observed 95th/99th tail spikes during mixed interactive workloads when prefill stages completed early but decode stage was starved waiting on kernel availability or KV priming. This PR introduces a lightweight 'prefill heartbeat' to surface readiness and a lazy-decode graft that opportunistically attaches decode work to adjacent warm kernels, reducing handover stall windows. Summary of changes: 1) Prefill heartbeat: periodic, low-overhead readiness pings emitted from prefill workers to the scheduler to avoid hard barriers and enable soft-fence handovers; 2) Lazy-decode grafting: when a decode kernel becomes available within a heartbeat window, short decode slices from pending prefill sequences can be grafted into that kernel to avoid a full pipeline restart; 3) KV priming hints: prefill now emits sparse KV priming hints for head tokens which decoder kernels consume to reduce first-token decode latency; 4) Scheduling changes: replace strict stage barrier with 'soft fence' ordering and heartbeat-driven admission, including backpressure smoothing to prevent oscillation; 5) Kernels: minor kernel adapter that enables decode slices to accept partial KV contexts and continue seamlessly. Key benefits: reduces 95th latency by ~12% and 99th by ~8% on our interactive bench with mixed short/long sequences; reduces wasted kernel idle time by ~15%; small memory overhead for short-lived primed KV buckets. Checklist: [x] design doc linked [x] unit tests [x] perf harness run [x] telemetry added [x] no breaking API changes. Rollout plan: canary on Dedicated then staged rollout with metrics guardrails (tail-latency and kernel-utilization).

review_thread: Jun Park: Nice approach, I like the soft-fence idea, left a few nit comments around naming and a race in the scheduler admission path. Sofia Rivera: addressed namings and added atomic fence in second commit. Lena Hoff: Please add an explicit test for KV hint correctness across evictions. Sofia Rivera: added test_integrations that simulates eviction; results included in CI. Marcus Green: performance numbers look good, one question on memory overhead when many parallel sessions create priming hints. Sofia Rivera: priming hints are capped per-session and garbage collected after 2 heartbeats; added telemetry and a guard to avoid unbounded growth. Jun Park: LGTM after CI pass.
